I used them winter stealth camping in the northern US. They were part of a system for heating my tent.

If the room is very cold (50ish or below), it's best to pre-heat it with some other source. Trying to heat a very cold room can thermal shock the clay, which leads to cracking.

I eventually just mounted a tin pan upside down over a large candle holder, that was enough to radiate heat into the tent for several hours. It also concealed the light, except for what would cast out the bottom, just enough to read a book. The candle could be transferred out for an alcohol burner as well. I crafted a second cooking alcohol burner as well. Cooking inside was a simple - insert the cooking burner, and use a small pot instead of the tin radiator pan.

You can mount almost any heat conductive material over a small fire source. Were I to build another one, i'd look for a cast iron pot.
